signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Strait of Hormuz Escalation
signals.text: Trump's declaration of the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. territory and subsequent Iranian threats create a massive safe-haven bid for JPY into the Sydney open. This geopolitical shock targets a rapid unwind of the JPY COT net short of -59.5k as the pair closed Friday at 159.31, below its SMA20 and SMA50. The escalation overrides the 264bp USD/JPY OIS carry advantage as markets price in maritime passage disruptions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY on safe-haven JPY demand. Catalyst: Sydney open at 21:00 UTC. Risk: De-escalation headlines or unexpected Fed hawkishness.
evidence: Trump: Pretty soon will be declaring Strait of Hormuz territory of the US

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Energy Supply Risk
signals.text: CAD emerges as the G10 leader with a 1W average of +1.079% (n=3) while JPY lags at -1.018% (n=7), creating a 2.097% spread that favors the cross. Crude oil's 1.42% Friday gain and Hormuz transit threats bolster the CAD/JPY +125bp carry advantage as CAD ESI (+10.3) outperforms JPY. The risk of a safe-haven JPY squeeze remains the primary headwind to this otherwise dominant trend. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY on energy-linked CAD strength. Catalyst: Sydney open at 21:00 UTC. Risk: JPY safe-haven spike on Strait of Hormuz military escalation.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded COT Long + Negative ESI Friction
signals.text: AUD COT LF net long +45.7k (74.6% long) creates significant crowded-long unwind risk if global risk sentiment sours over Middle East tensions. While AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7087 with a +73bp OIS carry advantage, the negative AUD ESI (-11.1) suggests data is already disappointing relative to the restrictive +0.55% real rate. The upcoming RBNZ meeting on 2 Sep may also drag on the AUD via regional proxy sentiment. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD on positioning unwind. Catalyst: Sydney open at 21:00 UTC. Risk: AUD/USD breaks above 0.7100 on broader USD weakness.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Retail Extreme + Divergent Options Skew
signals.text: GBP/USD retail sentiment is at a strong 75% short extreme, providing a contrarian bullish signal for a pair already trading above all major SMAs (20/50/200). GBP COT net long +42.7k (71.9% long) aligns with this trend, though the elevated +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV 6.0%) indicates heavy demand for downside protection. The neutral -11bp OIS carry differential makes the pair highly sensitive to the upcoming UK inflation data. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD on contrarian retail signals. Catalyst: Sydney open at 21:00 UTC. Risk: UK inflation miss triggers a pullback below SMA200 (1.3416).

signals.title: NZD/USD — Yield Advantage Compression
signals.text: NZD/USD closed at 0.5894 as a net short COT position of -34.031k (only 6% long) sets up a squeeze ahead of the RBNZ meeting on 2 Sep. NZD maintains the most accommodative real rate in the G10 at -1.56%, yet recent data beats (ESI +9.6) support the RBNZ's hiking bias. A USD/NZD carry disadvantage of +125bp (OIS) limits the upside unless USD breakdown risk materializes. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD on short-squeeze risk. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting on 2 Sep. Risk: NZD/USD falls below SMA20 (0.5849).
